playoff.entries: bottom two of the Opening Round plus bottom two of the Closing Round (4 clubs)
playoff.note: Knockout: the two losing teams are relegated, the two winners stay.

playoff.entries: 2nd vs 3rd only if level on points and goal difference
playoff.note: Normally the top two go up directly; in 2025-26 a tie forced a one-off play-off that Birżebbuġa won on penalties.

playoff.entries: 10th vs 11th only if level on points
playoff.note: Bottom four go down; in 2025-26 a tie for 10th/11th added a play-off for the fourth place.

boundaries.note: Challenge League top two go up. Premier League relegation is entirely play-off: the bottom two of the Opening Round and the bottom two of the Closing Round meet in a four-team knockout and the two losers go down.
National Amateur League I top two go up; Challenge League bottom two go down into it.

conflicts.real: Maltese Premier League (Opening Round is one half of its season)
conflicts.note: The league is a single competition of 12 clubs split into an Opening Round and a Closing Round, each with its own table and its own champion; points reset to zero between them. 'Opening Round' is not the league's name.
The Amateur League I had 14 clubs in 2025-26 (26 rounds) and drops to 12 for 2026-27 (22 rounds) after four relegations. Our 12 matches the coming season.

notes: Malta runs one August-May season. Premier League: 12 clubs, 11 rounds then a Top Six / Bottom Six split (5 more), then the whole thing again as the Closing Round with points reset - 16 matches per round, 32 per club per season. Champions and UEFA places are decided by comparing the two rounds, with a Final Four if different clubs win them (out of scope here). Challenge League: 16 clubs, 15 rounds then a Top Eight / Play-Out split (7 more) = 22. National Amateur League I: 12 clubs, 22 rounds, top two up, bottom four down (level 4, Amateur League II, not modelled). Level 1's downward route is a knockout, so 'bottom_n' would be wrong - the two worst clubs are not the two relegated.
